title: Rulings
html:
• Threat against survival: weights, with 2 or 3 presets along the curve ("Max threat", "Balanced", "Max survival"), like the PvP High HP preset. No death chance floor.
  • The survival score: healing needed (see Scoring survival). The project: "sometimes no amount of healing will work, if tank can be one-shotted". So the bench also reports the boss's biggest hit and the death floor, and a build that dies too often whatever the healing says so.
  • Forever's boss crit: audit which rule is more likely and go with it until a log confirms it. The audit below picks Forever's 0.6%.
  • The stand-in healer stays until the healing sim's healers heal, then tanks switch to them.
  • Tanks are scored on realistic raid encounters, not a generic boss: each one the boss's real damage on its tank and the healing such a raid puts on it, both tunable, the healing most of all, since it's our own group's (the project: "healing ... depends on our group which we control rather than the boss itself which we dont"). See Encounters.
  • Sources for boss and healing numbers, best first: Warcraft Logs from Season of Discovery, then the Anniversary realms (Vanilla, then TBC), then Classic Era, then private server cores like vmangos (docs/data_sources.md).
  • The optimizer's objective as proposed (see The optimizer's objective): SafeDPS against healing needed in raid DPS, healing needed by replay, presets at w = 1/3, 1 and 3.
  • Tanks keep 5% deaths for healing needed. The healing sim judges healers at under 2% tank deaths, a separate line for a separate score.

title: Encounters
html:
One set of boss encounters for the tank and healing sims (agreed with the healing sim session, 2026-11-02), in tools/encounters/<boss>.json (its README has the format). The tank bench reads them (-encounter), the heal bench not yet (it has its own -profile). Each file is a proto Encounter (the boss's melee, its abilities as raid damage events, tank swaps) and the healing a raid puts on its main tank, with the sources and the Warcraft Logs reports behind the numbers. The tank sim writes the tank side (the boss's melee, its abilities on the tank, the healing on the tank), the healing sim the raid damage.

The healing on the tank is set the way a raid sets it: healers on the tank, each one's healing per second on it, and their heals' cast time. Until healers heal, the bench turns that into the stand-in stream: their HPS added up, a heal every cast time over the healers, each one healer's heal. -healers, -healer-hps and -heal-cast change it for a run.

A boss's abilities on the tank are raid damage events aimed at the boss's target or the tanks. A melee one (Mortal Strike, Cleave, Hateful Strike) rolls the tank's miss, dodge, parry and block like a white swing, crits on its own roll and never crushes (melee, OutcomeEnemyMeleeSpecial), with no dual wield miss, and one can cut the healing taken for a while (healing_taken_multiplier, debuff_seconds, Mortal Strike's 50% for 5 s). A ticking event is never melee, and its debuff comes when it's applied. Not modelled yet: threat drops (Knock Away and the like), armor cuts (Corrosive Acid, Magma Splash), stacking DoTs (each stack is its own event), and abilities that scale with the boss's attack power (the files take Demoralizing Shout's cut off the weapon damage ones).

The seven (2026-11-02): Magmadar, Golemagg, Ragnaros, Onyxia, Broodlord Lashlayer, Vaelastrasz and Chromaggus, their tank side only. Forever's own raids (Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit, Onyxia) have no logs yet, so these are stand-ins.

Their numbers are Warcraft Logs' (2026-11-02). Tanks are scored on the Anniversary realms' set, tools/encounters/ (the project, 2026-11-02). tools/encounters/sod/ is the same bosses from Season of Discovery's Normal raids, first in the source order but tuned far above a pre-raid tank, kept to compare. From the logs: the boss's melee, his weapon damage abilities (Cleave, Mortal Strike, Knock Away), the fight's length, Elemental Fire's rate and the healing on the main tank. The other abilities keep the Classic Era client's spell data and the vmangos scripts' timers. tools/encounters/from_logs.py writes them from what wclcli.py tank mined (tools/encounters/logs/, with each sample of fights), and each file's source, reports and warcraftLogs say which kills.

  • What was checked first: wclcli.py tank on real reports. The boss's damage comes back only with hostilityType: Enemies (133 events against none without, SoD Onyxia), and the main tank's events have heal events with overheal (130 of 136) and absorbed events.
  • The fights are the newest public reports of each zone, not rankings: ranked fights are the fastest kills, and ranked reports from 2019 to 2024 are archived (their events need a paid account). Season of Discovery: 20 to 47 Normal kills a boss (2025 to 2026; Heroic and Mythic, the heat levels, hit up to 40% harder and are left out). Anniversary: 21 to 30 kills a boss from the realms' first months (Molten Core and Onyxia December 2024 to February 2025, Blackwing Lair March to July 2025), all 40 players.
  • The Anniversary logs are its Hardcore realms' (Doomhowl, Soulseeker, the same raids). Its Normal and PvP realms weren't found through the API: fresh serves the Classic progression realms' reports (tools/warcraftlogs/README.md). Era wasn't needed, both sources having all seven, and TBC has none of them.
  • Everything is measured while the boss is on the main tank: his swings on it no more than 6 s apart. Tank swaps, Onyxia's air phase and Ragnaros's knockbacks fall outside.
  • The melee is the median normal hit's unmitigatedAmount (before armor and before the crit or crushing multiplier), with the spread of each hit over its own kill's median (about 0.8 to 1.2 of it, close to Classic's ±14%: across kills the raids' debuffs on the boss differ). The swing gap is the mean while he's on the tank, parry haste and Frenzy in. Both are taken back through the debuffs the bench puts on him (tankbench -boss-stats: attack power 805 to 601, −37 a swing, attack speed 0.833), so under them he swings as in the logs. That assumes the logged raids had about the bench's debuffs.
  • The length is the kills' median, except Onyxia and Ragnaros (the main tank's time on him a kill) and Vaelastrasz (his longest stretch on one tank, one tank's stint).
  • The healing is the healers with 5% or more of the main tank's healing in the median kill, the healing it took from them with overheal and absorbs, and their heals and HoT ticks a second. The tank's own heals are left out (Season of Discovery's main tanks were mostly druids, warlocks and paladins, the Anniversary's warriors).
  • Golemagg's Double Attack goes: its swings log as white swings, so they're in the swing rate. Elemental Fire comes at the logs' rate: 18.9 a minute on the Anniversary realms (3 of 4 swings, the client's proc on landed hits), 5.5 in Season of Discovery's Normal.

What it shows:

  • Season of Discovery's Molten Core is near Classic's; its Onyxia and Blackwing Lair aren't. Its Normal Molten Core hits like the Anniversary's (and vmangos's). Its Onyxia hits twice as hard, and its Blackwing Lair 1.4 to 1.6 times, tuned for its own players: at Onyxia, Broodlord and Chromaggus its main tanks took 460 to 800 damage a second where ours take 920 to 1,380.

  • Season of Discovery's Broodlord is a one-shot for a pre-raid tank (7,000 health): his Mortal Strike lands for 7,000 to 11,500 through 56% armor. Its Onyxia and Chromaggus kill at the healing their raids gave their own, sturdier tanks. Scoring Forever's pre-raid tanks on them mostly measures that gap, so **tanks are scored on the Anniversary realms' set** (the project, 2026-11-02).
  • Healing needed under the damage taken (Golemagg, Magmadar) is the short fights: a 27 s kill takes about a quarter of a tank's health from its own pool.
  • Ragnaros on the Anniversary realms needs 2.3 times the damage taken, and its tanks took 725 a second where ours take 1,219: theirs wore fire resistance, which resists most of Elemental Fire (its ticks landed for 135 of 600).
  • Broodlord's Mortal Strike puts the death floor near 5% on the Anniversary realms (11,000 to 16,000 before armor), so healing needed there is unstable (its error is unbounded): a 7,000 health tank is near the line.

From the logs: tools/warcraftlogs/wclcli.py tank reads, per encounter, the boss's swings and abilities on the main tank, the tank's damage taken a second, and its healing taken (effective, overheal, absorbs, heals a second, healers, top heal spells). It needs a Warcraft Logs API client, on the project's machine or as WCL_CLIENT_ID and WCL_CLIENT_SECRET in a cloud environment. tools/warcraftlogs/README.md has where each realm's logs are.

title: The bench
html:
tools/tankbench sims tank requests (tools/tankbench/req/*.json, the DPS Report's request format with the tank as the first player) against a boss attacking the tank, with a stand-in healer:

``bash go run -tags=with_db ./tools/tankbench -iters 3000 tools/tankbench/req/*.json ``

  • The boss is the request's, the report's Level 60 boss by default (level 63, 2.0 s swing, about 3,975 to 4,975 before armor with its 805 attack power), or an encounter's (-encounter). -boss-level and -boss-damage change it, -dur the fight length.
  • The stand-in healer is the engine's healing model (below), at -hps (default 600) every -cadence seconds (2 ± -cadence-variation 1), or the encounter's healers (-healers, -healer-hps, -heal-cast), whose variation is half their cadence. It's the same trick as the raid sim's 700 TPS tank.
  • It prints the objective at the three presets, SafeDPS, healing needed at -death (5%) and the death floor, all from the one sim, then TPS, DPS, DTPS, TMI (-tmi-window 6 s), the chance of death, the sheet, and how the boss's swings landed over the fight. -actions adds threat by ability, -bisect checks the replay's healing needed by bisection over whole sims (about 10 more a build), -classic-crit gives the boss Classic's crit, and -dps-start, -dps-threat, -threat-members, -dps-slot and -healer-each set the objective.

The stand-in healer

One stream of heals, not healers (applyHealingModel, sim/core/health.go, from wowsims):

  • A heal lands every cadence seconds on average. With a variation, each gap is drawn from two even spreads either side of the cadence (2 ± 1 s: anywhere from 1 to 3 s).
  • Each heal is the HPS times the time since the last one. A long gap gets a big heal, so the healing per second is exact and only its timing is lumpy.
  • Healing over the tank's max health is lost. Healing taken modifiers apply.
  • Approximated: separate healers, cast times and heal sizes, as one stream whose heals are one healer's heal (an encounter's healers).
  • Not modelled: crits, shields, reacting to the tank's health (a healer who sees a big hit casts a fast heal), healers going out of mana. The heal comes whatever the tank's health, and stops for nothing.

What real raids look like: wowsims/forever's Classic Era Molten Core logs put the main tank's incoming healing at 2.4 times its damage taken, overhealing included, in heals about 0.3 s apart, 1.5% of it absorbs (their Protection warrior's OtherDefaults). So a real main tank is healed by several healers at once, far above its DTPS, and dies to a burst between heals rather than to running short on healing.

The real healers come from the healing sim (healing_sim.md): each healer's own spells, cast times, mana, shields and targets. Until then the stream is what scores tanks, and healing needed reads as "how much a steady healer would need", not as a healer comp.

First numbers (2026-11-02, 2,000 iterations, 180 s, 600 HPS, Forever's boss crit). Both builds wear the Classic Valor set, Mirah's Song and Draconian Deflector (ui/tank_warrior/gear_sets/p0.bis_sword_board, no neck, back, rings or trinkets), so these test the sim, not the classes:

BuildTPSDTPSTMIDeathEHCoverageCrush gapTook: blockedcrushed
Protection warrior1137431510%18,04846.6%53.4%59%1.4%
Protection paladin501497618.6%18,38936.7%63.3%23%12.3%

Shield Block keeps the warrior nearly uncrushable (2 blocks over 7 s on a 5 s cooldown). The paladin's Holy Shield was down most of the fight because its rotation was stale (fixed 2026-11-03, Rules audit); these numbers are from before.

The chance of death is a cliff at the tank's DTPS. The warrior dies in 98% of fights at 350 HPS, 65% at 425, 12% at 500 and none at 600. The paladin goes from 100% at 350 to 9% at 600. So one healer number mostly says where the cliff falls, and a small change in DTPS swings the result.

title: The stand-in healer
html:
One stream of heals, not healers (applyHealingModel, sim/core/health.go, from wowsims):

  • A heal lands every cadence seconds on average. With a variation, each gap is drawn from two even spreads either side of the cadence (2 ± 1 s: anywhere from 1 to 3 s).
  • Each heal is the HPS times the time since the last one. A long gap gets a big heal, so the healing per second is exact and only its timing is lumpy.
  • Healing over the tank's max health is lost. Healing taken modifiers apply.
  • Approximated: separate healers, cast times and heal sizes, as one stream whose heals are one healer's heal (an encounter's healers).

First numbers (2026-11-02, 2,000 iterations, 180 s, 600 HPS, Forever's boss crit). Both builds wear the Classic Valor set, Mirah's Song and Draconian Deflector (ui/tank_warrior/gear_sets/p0.bis_sword_board, no neck, back, rings or trinkets), so these test the sim, not the classes:

BuildTPSDTPSTMIDeathEHCoverageCrush gapTook: blockedcrushed
Protection warrior1137431510%18,04846.6%53.4%59%1.4%
Protection paladin501497618.6%18,38936.7%63.3%23%12.3%

Shield Block keeps the warrior nearly uncrushable (2 blocks over 7 s on a 5 s cooldown). The paladin's Holy Shield was down most of the fight because its rotation was stale (fixed 2026-11-03, Rules audit); these numbers are from before.

The chance of death is a cliff at the tank's DTPS. The warrior dies in 98% of fights at 350 HPS, 65% at 425, 12% at 500 and none at 600. The paladin goes from 100% at 350 to 9% at 600. So one healer number mostly says where the cliff falls, and a small change in DTPS swings the result.

Scoring survival

Healing needed (the rulings): the stand-in healer's HPS at which the tank dies in 5% of fights. It's one number per build that doesn't depend on picking a healer, and it counts both damage taken and spikes (a spiky build needs more healing to stay at 5%). TMI and DTPS stay next to it. It comes from a replay of each iteration (see The optimizer's objective), checked against the first version's bisection over whole sims: 611 against 611 for the paladin and 578 against 581 for the warrior at Onyxia, within the bisection's step.

Sometimes no healing is enough. A tank one swing can kill from full, or one a burst kills between two heals, dies whatever the healing. So the bench also reports:

  • The biggest hit (the sheet's) and how many of them the tank's health takes. Under 1 is a one-shot.
  • The death floor: the share of iterations the tank dies in even when every heal tops it off, so only damage between two heals kills it. Over 5%, healing needed is "none works", and the build isn't viable against that boss with that healer cadence.

The floor depends on the cadence. With 0.3 s heals it's lower than with 2 s heals, so the cadence is part of the scoring setup and stays fixed across builds.

The first numbers (1,000 iterations, the builds above):

BuildBoss critDTPSHealing neededDeath floorBiggest hitHits to kill
Protection warriorForever's431515 (1.20× DTPS)0%2,777 (a crushing blow)2.5
Protection paladinForever's497617 (1.24×)0%2,6972.6
Protection warriorClassic's433527 (1.22×)0%3,703 (a crit)1.9
Protection paladinClassic's518696 (1.34×)0%3,5961.9

Classic's crit costs the paladin far more than the warrior, since Shield Block pushes most crits off the warrior's table and the paladin's Holy Shield is down most of the fight.

The optimizer's objective

From a metrics review (2026-11-02, a subagent that read the bench and measured its noise), adopted by the user as proposed the same day, and built.

Score, in raid DPS: threat members × SafeDPS − w × DPS slot × healing needed / one healer's HPS.

  • Healing needed stays the survival number. DTPS gives Stamina no value, effective health ignores avoidance, TMI is a stand-in for what healing needed measures directly, and the chance of death at the encounter's own healing is a cliff (mostly 0% or near 100%) with little slope for a search to follow.
  • Computed by replay, not bisection. Without track_health the damage and the heal times don't depend on the HPS, only the heal sizes do. So one sim can record each iteration's damage and heal gaps and find the least HPS that iteration lives through. Healing needed is then a percentile of those, with no rounding step and with a standard error for the search's noise test, at a tenth of the cost. Measured: the bisection's step (1% of DTPS, 4.3 HPS for the warrior) is bigger than the sims' own noise (about 2.4 HPS over 6 seeds of 1,000 iterations). It's exact only while nothing reads the tank's health (health-based defensives and potions), which a scoring run turns off.
  • SafeDPS for threat: the steady DPS a reference DPS member can do without passing the tank at any moment of the fight, the mean over iterations of each one's lowest ratio. Passes come in the first seconds (raid_sim.md, Threat), which fight TPS hides, and a threat drop shows as a dip. Fight TPS stays as a column.
  • Both in raid DPS: a healer on the tank costs one DPS slot, and SafeDPS frees the DPS of the members close to the tank's threat (2 or 3). So w = 1 means one more healer costs one DPS player, which holds across bosses and gear. Presets: Max threat w = 1/3, Balanced 1, Max survival 3.
  • One hard reject: a death floor over 5% (no healing saves it).
  • The sheet's thresholds report and explain, they aren't scored. Their effect is already in the outcomes. Final presets are re-checked with -classic-crit, where a 440 Defense build can flip.

How it's built:

  • The engine (sim/core/tank_score.go): a player with tank_scoring (proto/common.proto) and the stand-in healer records each iteration's damage taken and heals, and at its end replays them to find the least stand-in HPS the iteration lives through (+Inf when none does). It also follows the tank's threat on the boss for SafeDPS: the reference member starts 2 s after the pull, makes 1 threat a point of damage (Forever removed Salvation, which made it 0.7) and pulls at 110%, all settable. Both land in UnitMetrics.tank_score, and core.TankScoreSummary turns the list into healing needed at a death share, its standard error (from the order statistics) and the death floor. A test checks that the replay agrees with the run itself: the iterations the run died in are exactly those whose least HPS is over the healer's.
  • The objective (tools/tankscore): the encounter files, setting a request up as a tank, and the score with its standard error, shared by the bench and rotopt. A build no healing saves at 5% scores far below any other (−1,000,000, lower the more often it dies), so a search still climbs out of it.
  • rotopt -tank max-threat|balanced|max-survival (or a weight) scores the player as a tank in place of DPS, so every search (rotation knobs, gear, talents) maximizes it, against -tank-encounter (whose fight length is the default -durs) or a 600 HPS healer (-tank-hps). -tank-threat-members, -tank-dps-slot and -tank-death set the rest.

First search (2026-11-02): rotopt's talent search on the warrior at Broodlord, Balanced, 600 iterations a candidate and 3,000 to confirm (248 sims). It kept the build. Its best swap, Improved Thunder Clap's 3 points into Cruelty for more threat (SafeDPS 1,487 to 1,517), gained 73 ± 43, short of the search's two standard errors. Healing needed is noisy where one ability makes the bad fights: ±15 HPS at 3,000 iterations at Broodlord (Mortal Strike's healing cut), against ±3 at Onyxia. Two candidates share the random seed, so their difference is far less noisy than the two errors added up, which is what the search's test assumed.

The paired test (2026-11-02): every rotopt search (knobs, talents, gear, enchants) now tests a tank candidate's gain against the error of its difference from the best, iteration by iteration (tankscore.PairedDiff). Two runs share their seed and iterations, and the engine keeps each iteration's SafeDPS and least HPS in seed order (TankScore.safe_dps_each, survive_hps), so iteration k of two runs had the same rolls up to where the builds differ. The error is a bootstrap: 400 resamples of the iterations, the same ones for both runs. It falls back to the two errors added up when the runs don't pair, over several fight lengths, or near the death floor (more than a tenth of the resamples with no healing that saves the tank). Checked against the real spread of the difference over 10 seeds (1,000 iterations, the warrior, the Anniversary files):

EncounterBuildsSpread over seedsPaired errorErrors added up
Onyxiawithout Strength of Earth Totem0.71.257.8
Chromagguswithout Strength of Earth Totem0.50.834.9
Onyxiawithout Power Word: Fortitude12.920.457.1
Chromagguswithout Power Word: Fortitude22.519.439.9

So the search's noise drops 2 to 50 times, least where survival moves. At Broodlord the pre-raid warrior sits on the death floor (4.5%), where healing needed has no finite error and nothing pairs: a search there needs a sturdier tank or more healing.

First search with it (2026-11-02): the warrior's talent search at Chromaggus (Anniversary), Balanced, 600 iterations a candidate and 3,000 to confirm (789 sims, 73 s). It took Improved Thunder Clap's 3 points into Cruelty (+66, noise 8: the swap the Broodlord search couldn't tell from noise), then Improved Shield Wall's 2 (+22, noise 7.7), to 35-05-251530120331201351. Both moves are the sim's gaps, not findings yet: the bench's requests give the boss Improved Thunder Clap as a raid debuff whatever the tank takes, and a scoring run has no health-based defensives, so Shield Wall and Last Stand can't pay. Many talents score exactly the same (Iron Will, Lingering Rage, Booming Voice), the sim not reading them. So the rules audit (Next steps, 1) comes before the presets' searches: the debuffs a tank brings itself have to come from its own talents.

Not modelled yet, which the score would reward once it is: threat drops from boss abilities (Knock Away), and a tank's own health-based effects, which the replay can't follow (health potions, defensives at a health share, APL conditions on health). A scoring run leaves those out.

Open decisions

None for the objective. The weights of the presets get checked once the gear search runs on them (two presets landing on the same build means a weight moves).

Findings so far

  • The DPS Report's requests give the raid Salvation (raid.buffs.salvation, −30% threat). Copied into a tank's request it cut the warrior from 1137 to 794 TPS. The bench's requests drop it.
  • The raid sim's 700 TPS stand-in came from the warrior's tank suite. On the report's boss with no Salvation the same build does 1137. Check which buffs the 700 had before the raid sim's simmed tanks replace it.
  • The Protection paladin's rotation was stale (Holy Shield only while Redoubt was up, no Holy Strike). The bench's is fixed (Rules audit); its options still need Righteous Fury on (righteousFury).
  • The Feral tank wasn't simmed at all (WotLK code left out of the build). It's rebuilt for Forever (Rules audit).
  • The paladin and the Warden shaman have no gear (blank sets only), and no tank has Forever synthetic gear or a tuned rotation.
  • Armor had no cap. Armor now takes off at most 75% (GetArmorDamageModifier). Nothing simmed before got near it.

Rules audit

Protection warrior (2026-11-02), every talent a tank build can reach against Forever's client data (build 70707 with the realms' hotfixes) and forever-wiki/classes/warrior.md:

  • Right in the sim: Shield Specialization (1% block and a 20% chance of 5 Rage on a block, a point), Anticipation (4 Defense a point), Improved Bloodrage, Master of Defense, Improved Revenge (20% a point), Defiance (5% a point, with a shield), Improved Sunder Armor, Improved Shield Wall (5.5 min a point), Focused Rage, Bastion (2% Physical a point, with a shield), Deflection, Cruelty, Booming Voice.
  • Fixed: Blood Craze (Fury row 3) wasn't simmed. It heals 1 / 2 / 3% of max health over 6 s after a crit taken, a hit over 20% of max health or Bloodthirst (client 70707: 16487 triggers 16488, 3 ticks 2 s apart). Under Forever's 0.6% boss crit, it's the big hits: a crushing blow on a pre-raid tank is about 20% of its health. At Chromaggus it procs 17 times a fight and heals about 2,400, but moves healing needed by nothing measurable (905 to 910 ± 7), since the bad fights are bursts it's too slow for. The picker no longer marks it as not simulated.
  • Not simmed, and rightly worth nothing in a boss fight: Iron Will, Improved Disarm, Improved Shield Bash, Concussion Blow (worth only as Shield Slam's prerequisite), Lingering Rage, Piercing Howl. Gore Drinker needs Enrage 5/5, out of a tank's reach.
  • Worth something in game, nothing in the score yet:
    • Thunder Clap and Demoralizing Shout were the raid's: the bench's requests gave the boss both whoever cast them, and the tank's rotation cast neither, so Improved Thunder Clap and Booming Voice were worth nothing and the first talent search dropped Improved Thunder Clap for Cruelty. **The project's ruling (2026-11-02): the tank applies them.** So a warrior tank's bench and rotopt runs drop Thunder Clap, Demoralizing Shout and Demoralizing Roar (it doesn't stack with the Shout) from the raid's debuffs (tankscore.OwnDebuffs), and the bench's warrior refreshes Demoralizing Shout under 3 s left and Thunder Clap under 2 s, right after Shield Block. They're up 101% and 96% of the fight at Chromaggus, and the boss has the same attack power and swing speed at 30 s as with the raid's (tankbench -boss-stats: 601 and 0.833), so the encounter files' calibration holds. The cost: 30 to 80 TPS on the seven bosses, SafeDPS at Chromaggus 1,811 to 1,494 (the opening GCDs go to the debuffs), and 0 to 30 more damage taken a second (the seconds before they're up). The Chromaggus talent search now keeps the build: its best swap, Improved Heroic Strike into Cruelty, gains 28 ± 14.4, short of two errors.
    • Last Stand, Shield Wall and Improved Shield Wall: real tanks save them for a bad moment, which a scoring run can't follow (the replay needs nothing to read the tank's health). Shield Wall on a timer would undervalue it.
    • Vanguard: Charge in Defensive Stance, a Rage opener at the pull. The tank's rotation doesn't charge; it's the rotations' work (Next steps, 3).

Protection paladin (2026-11-03), the bench's build -55302102513521531-052 against forever-wiki/classes/paladin.md (the client rows of 70707 with its hotfixes):

  • Right in the sim: Redoubt, Improved Righteous Fury, Shield Specialization, Iron Creed, Sacred Duty, Holy Shield, Reckoning, Anticipation, Toughness, Precision, Divine Intellect, Swift Judgement, and Shieldsworn (simmed in holy_strike.go; the picker marked it not simulated, now fixed).
  • Not simmed, and worth nothing on a boss: Stoicism (shorter stuns and charms), Improved Hammer of Justice, Guardian's Favor (Blessing of Protection and Freedom).
  • Worth something in game, nothing in the score: Templar's Bulwark (an absorb of the paladin's whole health for 8 s, 5 min cooldown, Forbearance), an emergency button like Shield Wall that a scoring run can't follow; Eye for an Eye, which needs the boss's crits (0.6% under Forever).
  • Fixed: the bench's rotation. It cast Holy Shield only while Redoubt was up, and never Holy Strike, which Iron Creed and Shieldsworn are about. It now keeps Holy Shield up and casts Holy Strike on cooldown (6 s with Shieldsworn), then the seal, Judgement and Consecration as before. On the seven Anniversary bosses its TPS goes up about half (611 to 929 at Chromaggus), its damage taken down 4 to 7%, and its healing needed down 6 to 47% (Broodlord 2,541 to 1,344, Ragnaros 2,961 to 2,273). Holy Shield's 4 charges go in 4 blocks, so it still takes 12% crushing blows. The UI preset's rotation is the rotations step's.

Feral tank (2026-11-03): brought into the build. Its code was WotLK's (Maul 48480, Savage Defense, Mangle) and left out, and Bear Form itself was commented out. It's rebuilt for Forever (sim/druid/bear.go, bear_attacks.go, sim/druid/tank, its test TestForeverBear), from client 70707 with its hotfixes and, where the client is silent, wowsims/forever's bear (forever-wiki/classes/druid.md, The bear, has every value): Dire Bear Form (+360% armor from items, +1,240 health, +180 attack power, 1.5x threat, the weapon's DPS at 2.5 s with a two-hander's Rage), Maul, Swipe, Demoralizing Roar, Enrage, Frenzied Regeneration, Lacerate and Primal Bite, and the bear's talents (Thick Hide, Heart of the Wild, Natural Reaction, Blood Frenzy, Feral Instinct, Savage Fury, Rend and Tear).

  • Assumed until a log of a bear tank: none of its attacks has threat beyond the form's 1.5x (2.15x under the November 2 notes; Classic's Maul and Swipe had 1.75); Enrage's armor cut is the tooltip's 16% (the client's 25503 says 26%); Thick Hide's Defense part (0.67 a point) is the tooltip's.
  • The bench's bear (then druid_bear.json; since 2026-11-04 the three presets druid_bear_{max_threat,balanced,max_survival}.json on the bear's own synthetic set, docs/tank_druid.md) wore the Feral cat's synthetic set, so 507 Agility, 35% dodge and 8,900 health; a bear set is the gear step's. It keeps its own Demoralizing Roar up (tankscore.OwnDebuffs drops the raid's Roar and Shout), then Primal Bite, Lacerate to 5 stacks and Maul at 30 Rage. Not in its rotation yet: Enrage (its armor cut makes it a pull-time choice), Frenzied Regeneration (an emergency button, like Shield Wall), Swipe (single target).
  • On the seven Anniversary bosses it makes about 900 TPS (the paladin's level, the warrior's 1,150), takes 5 to 15% more damage than the plate tanks (no block or parry, 15% crushing blows) and the biggest hits (2,000 to 4,000), and has the lowest death floor at Broodlord (0.9%, 8,900 health):

Next steps

  1. Rules audit of the Warden shaman like the others above (it needs gear first). Bring the Feral tank into the build. Ask for a dungeon boss log for Forever's boss crit.
  2. Encounters: Patchwerk, threat drops, armor cuts and stacking DoTs in the engine.
  3. Rotations: the paladin's and the Warden's first, then rotopt templates for all four.
  4. The three presets' searches (the paired test is in, above).
  5. Tank gear: a tank row in orchestration/gear_targets.md and synthetic tank items, then gear and talent searches on the score.
  6. The report: a tank section with TPS next to damage taken, healing needed and the sheet's thresholds.
  7. The raid sim: the simmed tank's threat in place of the 700 TPS stand-in, then the comp search.

Audits

Four auditors checked the work on 2026-11-02, each starting cold, and their findings are fixed:

  • Engine: the tank sheet matches the rolled outcomes within noise over 60,000 swings a case, the armor cap moves no existing result, and classic_crit works end to end. Fixed: a boss ability's blocked crit was booked twice, its miss took the white swing's dual wield 19%, a dual wielding boss crashed the sim (no off hand attack table for enemies, older than this work), a ticking event dropped its debuff, and the biggest hit left out flat damage and damage taken. Open: the cores may roll a melee ability's block after the avoidance, not on the same roll.
  • Bench and log miner: the bisection is valid (the chance of death moves only with the HPS, checked over sweeps). Fixed: the death floor at 20 times DTPS didn't always top the tank off (now 1,000), "none works" at a reachable target, an HPS of 0 starting the engine's presim healer, the encounter dropping the request's execute phases, half-set healer flags, and in the miner the boss's events needing hostilityType: Enemies, results lost when the budget ran out mid-sample, and absorbs left out of the healing ratio.
  • Encounter data: every spell value matches the Classic Era client's spell tables, and the timers the vmangos scripts. Fixed: Broodlord's weapon damage (above), Vaelastrasz's stacking breath, Double Attack's and Elemental Fire's rates, Demoralizing Shout on weapon damage abilities, first casts, Onyxia's notes.
  • This doc against the code: every number matched. Fixed: the resistance formula, the swing range of the report's boss, the biggest hit's scope, the uncrushable test's crit, aura 20134, stale lines.

title: Scoring survival
html:
Healing needed (the rulings): the stand-in healer's HPS at which the tank dies in 5% of fights. It's one number per build that doesn't depend on picking a healer, and it counts both damage taken and spikes (a spiky build needs more healing to stay at 5%). TMI and DTPS stay next to it. It comes from a replay of each iteration (see The optimizer's objective), checked against the first version's bisection over whole sims: 611 against 611 for the paladin and 578 against 581 for the warrior at Onyxia, within the bisection's step.

Sometimes no healing is enough. A tank one swing can kill from full, or one a burst kills between two heals, dies whatever the healing. So the bench also reports:

  • The biggest hit (the sheet's) and how many of them the tank's health takes. Under 1 is a one-shot.
  • The death floor: the share of iterations the tank dies in even when every heal tops it off, so only damage between two heals kills it. Over 5%, healing needed is "none works", and the build isn't viable against that boss with that healer cadence.

The floor depends on the cadence. With 0.3 s heals it's lower than with 2 s heals, so the cadence is part of the scoring setup and stays fixed across builds.

The first numbers (1,000 iterations, the builds above):

BuildBoss critDTPSHealing neededDeath floorBiggest hitHits to kill
Protection warriorForever's431515 (1.20× DTPS)0%2,777 (a crushing blow)2.5
Protection paladinForever's497617 (1.24×)0%2,6972.6
Protection warriorClassic's433527 (1.22×)0%3,703 (a crit)1.9
Protection paladinClassic's518696 (1.34×)0%3,5961.9

Classic's crit costs the paladin far more than the warrior, since Shield Block pushes most crits off the warrior's table and the paladin's Holy Shield is down most of the fight.

title: The score
html:
From a metrics review (2026-11-02, a subagent that read the bench and measured its noise), adopted by the user as proposed the same day, and built.

Score, in raid DPS: threat members × SafeDPS − w × DPS slot × healing needed / one healer's HPS.

  • Healing needed stays the survival number. DTPS gives Stamina no value, effective health ignores avoidance, TMI is a stand-in for what healing needed measures directly, and the chance of death at the encounter's own healing is a cliff (mostly 0% or near 100%) with little slope for a search to follow.
  • Computed by replay, not bisection. Without track_health the damage and the heal times don't depend on the HPS, only the heal sizes do. So one sim can record each iteration's damage and heal gaps and find the least HPS that iteration lives through. Healing needed is then a percentile of those, with no rounding step and with a standard error for the search's noise test, at a tenth of the cost. Measured: the bisection's step (1% of DTPS, 4.3 HPS for the warrior) is bigger than the sims' own noise (about 2.4 HPS over 6 seeds of 1,000 iterations). It's exact only while nothing reads the tank's health (health-based defensives and potions), which a scoring run turns off.
  • SafeDPS for threat: the steady DPS a reference DPS member can do without passing the tank at any moment of the fight, the mean over iterations of each one's lowest ratio. Passes come in the first seconds (raid_sim.md, Threat), which fight TPS hides, and a threat drop shows as a dip. Fight TPS stays as a column.
  • Both in raid DPS: a healer on the tank costs one DPS slot, and SafeDPS frees the DPS of the members close to the tank's threat (2 or 3). So w = 1 means one more healer costs one DPS player, which holds across bosses and gear. Presets: Max threat w = 1/3, Balanced 1, Max survival 3.
  • One hard reject: a death floor over 5% (no healing saves it).
  • The sheet's thresholds report and explain, they aren't scored. Their effect is already in the outcomes. Final presets are re-checked with -classic-crit, where a 440 Defense build can flip.

How it's built:

  • The engine (sim/core/tank_score.go): a player with tank_scoring (proto/common.proto) and the stand-in healer records each iteration's damage taken and heals, and at its end replays them to find the least stand-in HPS the iteration lives through (+Inf when none does). It also follows the tank's threat on the boss for SafeDPS: the reference member starts 2 s after the pull, makes 1 threat a point of damage (Forever removed Salvation, which made it 0.7) and pulls at 110%, all settable. Both land in UnitMetrics.tank_score, and core.TankScoreSummary turns the list into healing needed at a death share, its standard error (from the order statistics) and the death floor. A test checks that the replay agrees with the run itself: the iterations the run died in are exactly those whose least HPS is over the healer's.
  • The objective (tools/tankscore): the encounter files, setting a request up as a tank, and the score with its standard error, shared by the bench and rotopt. A build no healing saves at 5% scores far below any other (−1,000,000, lower the more often it dies), so a search still climbs out of it.
  • rotopt -tank max-threat|balanced|max-survival (or a weight) scores the player as a tank in place of DPS, so every search (rotation knobs, gear, talents) maximizes it, against -tank-encounter (whose fight length is the default -durs) or a 600 HPS healer (-tank-hps). -tank-threat-members, -tank-dps-slot and -tank-death set the rest.

First search (2026-11-02): rotopt's talent search on the warrior at Broodlord, Balanced, 600 iterations a candidate and 3,000 to confirm (248 sims). It kept the build. Its best swap, Improved Thunder Clap's 3 points into Cruelty for more threat (SafeDPS 1,487 to 1,517), gained 73 ± 43, short of the search's two standard errors. Healing needed is noisy where one ability makes the bad fights: ±15 HPS at 3,000 iterations at Broodlord (Mortal Strike's healing cut), against ±3 at Onyxia. Two candidates share the random seed, so their difference is far less noisy than the two errors added up, which is what the search's test assumed.

The paired test (2026-11-02): every rotopt search (knobs, talents, gear, enchants) now tests a tank candidate's gain against the error of its difference from the best, iteration by iteration (tankscore.PairedDiff). Two runs share their seed and iterations, and the engine keeps each iteration's SafeDPS and least HPS in seed order (TankScore.safe_dps_each, survive_hps), so iteration k of two runs had the same rolls up to where the builds differ. The error is a bootstrap: 400 resamples of the iterations, the same ones for both runs. It falls back to the two errors added up when the runs don't pair, over several fight lengths, or near the death floor (more than a tenth of the resamples with no healing that saves the tank). Checked against the real spread of the difference over 10 seeds (1,000 iterations, the warrior, the Anniversary files):

EncounterBuildsSpread over seedsPaired errorErrors added up
Onyxiawithout Strength of Earth Totem0.71.257.8
Chromagguswithout Strength of Earth Totem0.50.834.9
Onyxiawithout Power Word: Fortitude12.920.457.1
Chromagguswithout Power Word: Fortitude22.519.439.9

So the search's noise drops 2 to 50 times, least where survival moves. At Broodlord the pre-raid warrior sits on the death floor (4.5%), where healing needed has no finite error and nothing pairs: a search there needs a sturdier tank or more healing.

First search with it (2026-11-02): the warrior's talent search at Chromaggus (Anniversary), Balanced, 600 iterations a candidate and 3,000 to confirm (789 sims, 73 s). It took Improved Thunder Clap's 3 points into Cruelty (+66, noise 8: the swap the Broodlord search couldn't tell from noise), then Improved Shield Wall's 2 (+22, noise 7.7), to 35-05-251530120331201351. Both moves are the sim's gaps, not findings yet: the bench's requests give the boss Improved Thunder Clap as a raid debuff whatever the tank takes, and a scoring run has no health-based defensives, so Shield Wall and Last Stand can't pay. Many talents score exactly the same (Iron Will, Lingering Rage, Booming Voice), the sim not reading them. So the rules audit (Next steps, 1) comes before the presets' searches: the debuffs a tank brings itself have to come from its own talents.

Not modelled yet, which the score would reward once it is: threat drops from boss abilities (Knock Away), and a tank's own health-based effects, which the replay can't follow (health potions, defensives at a health share, APL conditions on health). A scoring run leaves those out.
